stage: preregistration, committed before physics/skyrmion_check.py is run on the data
question: Do real, experimentally measured 2D point configurations respect the energy bound that D2 (+ upstream universal_energy_minimum) states for every configuration of the same density?
data: Zenodo record 4450305 (CC-BY-4.0), 'Skyrmion Lattice Phases in Thin Film Multilayer' (arXiv:2004.09244): Kerr-microscopy skyrmion positions, snapshots fig3/FIG_snap_absPsi6_330K_40uT.dat (1618 points) and fig3/FIG_snap_absPsi6_338K_20uT.dat (4224 points); columns x [um], y [um], |psi6|. File checksums verified against the Zenodo API before use.
why_this_is_a_test_of_the_statement: D2 bounds the energy of EVERY locally finite configuration of density rho, for EVERY completely monotone g of squared distance. It does not depend on the system's true interaction, so any measured point pattern is a legitimate input. Short-range Gaussians g_alpha(t) = exp(-pi alpha t) (density-1 units) make the window estimate local; Riesz s = 3, 4, 6 (t^{-s/2}, informative for s > 2 by D1b) test the physically familiar dipolar-like (s = 3) case with a continuum tail correction.
estimator: Rescale coordinates by sqrt(rho_hat) (density-1 units). Window = axis-aligned bounding box of the points; inner box = window shrunk by R_c = 6 on every side; rho_hat = (points in inner box) / (inner-box area), iterated once after rescaling. Per-point energy of each inner point x: sum over all data points y with 0 < |x - y| < R_c of g(|x - y|^2), plus for Riesz the uniform-density tail 2 pi R_c^{2-s} / (s - 2). E_emp = mean over inner points. E_lat = sum over the density-1 triangular lattice A minus 0 of g(|a|^2) (direct sum, truncation < 1e-10).
prediction: For both snapshots and all 7 potentials (Gaussian alpha in {0.5, 1, 2, 4}; Riesz s in {3, 4, 6}): relative gap (E_emp - E_lat) / E_lat >= -tol, where tol is calibrated BEFORE looking at the data: tol = 3 x max |relative gap| of control C1 over 20 random orientations/offsets of a perfect triangular patch with the same point count and window aspect ratio as the respective snapshot.
kill_criterion: Any snapshot/potential with relative gap < -tol is reported as a FAIL (a measured configuration below the triangular-lattice bound beyond finite-size error) and investigated, never dropped. Also FAIL if any control below behaves contrary to its stated expectation, since then the estimator is not trustworthy.

controls.C1_perfect_lattice: perfect triangular patch, same N and window aspect: |gap| <= tol/3 by construction (it calibrates tol); reported
controls.C2_jittered_lattice: triangular patch with Gaussian jitter sigma in {0.05, 0.1, 0.2} (density-1 units): gap > tol and increasing with sigma for every potential
controls.C3_square_lattice: square patch: gap > tol; for Riesz s = 4 the gap should be close to 6.02681/5.78336 - 1 = 4.21% (closed forms from verification/D1)
controls.C4_density_mismatch: evaluate the real data against the lattice at density 1.3 rho_hat instead of rho_hat (the analogue of unscaled_false): at least one potential must show gap < -tol, i.e. the test is able to fail

exploratory_not_gated: Spearman correlation between each inner skyrmion's local Gaussian (alpha = 1) energy excess over the lattice and its measured |psi6|; expected negative (more disordered neighbourhoods carry more energy).
what_a_pass_does_not_mean: A pass is consistency evidence (Tier X) that the formal statement's physical reading is not contradicted by real data. It does not test the upstream proof, does not establish that skyrmions interact through a completely monotone potential, and a finite window is not the liminf over growing disks that the theorem is about.
probability_estimate: ~90% pass (prior; real 2D lattices are known to sit above the ideal lattice energy), main risk = estimator bias at the window edge or density misestimation
